q: Who is the author of the chapter "Naubaatkhane mein Ibaadat"?
e: "Naubaatkhane mein Ibaadat" is a biographical sketch written by noted author and music connoisseur Yatindra Mishra.

q: Under which prose genre does "Naubaatkhane mein Ibaadat" fall?
e: This chapter is a biographical sketch (vyaktichitra) based on the life and personality of shehnai maestro Ustad Bismillah Khan.

q: What was the childhood name of Ustad Bismillah Khan?
e: Ustad Bismillah Khan’s childhood name was Amiruddin; he was born in Dumraon.

q: At which place was Bismillah Khan born?
e: Amiruddin (Bismillah Khan) was born in a music-loving family in Dumraon, Bihar.

q: Of which musical instrument was Bismillah Khan a world-renowned player?
e: Ustad Bismillah Khan was a world-famous shehnai maestro and a Bharat Ratna awardee.

q: At the beginning of the chapter, around 1916–1922 in Kashi, what is Amiruddin’s age mentioned as?
e: The chapter mentions that Amiruddin is only six years old while his elder brother Shamsuddin is nine.

q: What was the name of Amiruddin’s elder brother?
e: Amiruddin’s elder brother was named Shamsuddin, who was nine years old at the opening of the text.

q: What was the name of Bismillah Khan’s father?
e: Bismillah Khan’s father was Ustad Paigambar Bakhsh Khan and his mother’s name was Mitthan.

q: What was the name of Bismillah Khan’s mother?
e: The text introduces Amiruddin as the younger son of Ustad Paigambar Bakhsh Khan and Mitthan of Dumraon.

q: How was Ustad Salar Hussain Khan related to Amiruddin?
e: According to the text, Ustad Salar Hussain Khan, a resident of Dumraon, was Amiruddin’s great-grandfather.

q: What is the correct meaning of the word "Naubaatkhana"?
o: A gallery above the entrance gate where auspicious music is played
e: A Naubaatkhana is a pavilion above an entrance gate where auspicious instruments like shehnai and kettledrums are played.

q: What does the word "Ibaadat" mean?
e: "Ibaadat" means worship or prayer; for Khan Sahib, playing the shehnai was itself a form of worship.

q: At the threshold of which temple in Kashi did Amiruddin’s two maternal uncles play the shehnai?
e: Amiruddin’s maternal uncles Sadiq Hussain and Alibakhsh played the shehnai at the threshold of the Balaji Temple in Kashi.

q: In which city was Amiruddin’s maternal home (nanihal)?
e: At the age of five or six, Amiruddin left his birthplace Dumraon to live at his maternal home in Kashi.

q: What material is used to make the "reed" of a shehnai?
e: The reed fitted into a shehnai for blowing is made from a hollow grass called "narkat".

q: Along the banks of which river is "narkat" found in Dumraon?
e: The narkat grass used to make shehnai reeds grows along the banks of the Son river in Dumraon.

q: In Arab countries, what is a wind instrument played with a reed called?
e: In Arab lands, a reed-based wind instrument is called "Nay", and the shehnai is called "Shahe-Nay".

q: What does the title "Shahe-Nay" mean?
e: The shehnai is given the title "Shahe-Nay", meaning the king among wind (sushir) instruments.

q: While going to the Balaji temple, passing by which two singer sisters’ house did Amiruddin enjoy?
e: Amiruddin loved passing by the house of Rasoolan Bai and Batoolan Bai to hear their thumri, tappa, and dadra.

q: In which year did Ustad Bismillah Khan receive India’s highest civilian honour, the Bharat Ratna?
e: Ustad Bismillah Khan was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2001 for his unparalleled contribution to music.

q: When and where was Yatindra Mishra born?
e: Yatindra Mishra was born in 1977 in Ayodhya (Uttar Pradesh) and completed his M.A. in Hindi from Lucknow University.

q: On the life of which renowned classical singer did Yatindra Mishra write the book "Girija"?
e: Yatindra Mishra wrote the book "Girija" on the life and musical devotion of classical vocalist Girija Devi.

q: For how many days of Muharram did neither Bismillah Khan nor anyone in his family play the shehnai?
e: The ten days of Muharram are days of mourning, so during these ten days none of them played the shehnai.

q: In which confectioner’s kachoris did Amiruddin hear music?
e: When Kulsum the confectioner dropped kachoris into boiling ghee, Amiruddin heard musical ascent and descent in the sizzling sound.

q: Which actress’s films was Bismillah Khan especially fond of?
e: Bismillah Khan was a great fan of actresses Sulochana and Geeta Bali, and used to buy third-class tickets to watch their films.

q: What did Bismillah Khan pray for from God after all five daily prayers (namaz)?
e: Even at the age of eighty, after every five daily prayers, Bismillah Khan asked God solely for the blessing of a true musical note.

q: On the occasion of Hanuman Jayanti in Kashi, at which temple was a five-day classical and semi-classical music festival held?
e: At the Sankatmochan Temple in Kashi, an extraordinary five-day classical and semi-classical music gathering was held on Hanuman Jayanti.

q: Which river in Kashi did Bismillah Khan affectionately address as "Ganga Maiya"?
e: Bismillah Khan called the Ganga river in Kashi "Ganga Maiya" with deep reverence and never wished to leave Kashi.

q: What were the names of Bismillah Khan’s two maternal uncles?
e: Amiruddin’s two maternal uncles, Sadiq Hussain and Alibakhsh, were renowned shehnai players of the country.

q: When and at what age did Ustad Bismillah Khan pass away?
e: Bharat Ratna Ustad Bismillah Khan passed away on 21 August 2006 at the age of 90.

q: In Indian musicology, under which category of instruments is the shehnai classified?
e: Perforated instruments played by blowing air are called "sushir vadya"; the shehnai belongs to this category.

q: Which instrument is NOT mentioned in Tansen’s composition from the late 16th century found in "Sangeet Raag Kalpadrum"?
e: Tansen’s composition preserved in Sangeet Raag Kalpadrum mentions murli, vanshi, shringi, and murchang, but not the shehnai.

q: In Indian tradition, how is the shehnai regarded among musical instruments?
e: In India, the shehnai is considered the foremost instrument of auspicious ceremonies, weddings, and sacred rituals.

q: On the eighth day of Muharram, approximately how far did Bismillah Khan walk in Dalmandi near Fatman while playing the nauha?
e: On the eighth day of Muharram, Khan Sahib walked eight kilometres on foot with tearful eyes, playing the mournful nauha.

q: When Amiruddin went to cinema halls in Kashi buying a third-class ticket, what was the price of the ticket?
e: A third-class ticket cost six paise, which Amiruddin collected by taking two paise from his mamu, two from his mausi, and two from his nani.

q: From which three relatives did Amiruddin get two paise each to buy his cinema ticket?
o: Maternal uncle (mamu), maternal aunt (mausi), and maternal grandmother (nani)
e: In his childhood, Amiruddin took two paise each from his mamu, mausi, and nani to buy a six-paise ticket for Sulochana’s new film.

q: In the 1930s, what did Amiruddin receive as remuneration for playing the shehnai at the Balaji Temple?
e: For playing the shehnai at the threshold of the Balaji temple, Amiruddin earned a chavanni (four-anna coin), which he spent on films.

q: When maternal uncle Alibakhsh Khan hit the beat (sam) while playing the shehnai, what did Amiruddin strike on the ground?
e: Whenever Alibakhsh Khan arrived at the sam while playing, young Amiruddin slammed a stone onto the ground in appreciation.

q: Listening to whom in childhood did Amiruddin develop the sense of applauding at the musical "sam"?
o: Maternal uncle Alibakhsh Khan’s shehnai playing
e: When uncle Alibakhsh Khan hit the sam at the Balaji temple, Amiruddin responded by striking a stone, honing his sense of rhythm.

q: In the context of the chapter, what does the word "tahmad" mean?
e: "Tahmad" refers to a lungi or unstitched lower garment, which Bismillah Khan comfortably wore at home.

q: In what context did Bismillah Khan pray to God saying "do not grant me a cracked note (phata sur)"?
o: When a disciple pointed out his torn lungi (tahmad)
When he went to Delhi for the Bharat Ratna
e: When a disciple remarked on his torn lungi, he replied that the Bharat Ratna was for his shehnai; clothes can be mended, only the musical note must never crack.

q: In Kashi, facing which direction did Bismillah Khan bow in prayer (sajda) as a mark of devotion?
o: Towards Kashi Vishwanath and Balaji Temple
e: Even when away from Kashi, he would sit facing the direction of Kashi Vishwanath and Balaji Temple and turn his shehnai that way.

q: To which area of Kashi does the term "Pakka Mahal" refer?
o: The old traditional residential quarter adjacent to Kashi Vishwanath
e: Pakka Mahal is the oldest densely built neighbourhood adjoining Kashi Vishwanath, famous for its malai baraf and traditional culture.

q: According to Yatindra Mishra, what was remarkable about Kashi’s music gatherings and culture?
o: Only foreign instruments were played there
Music was restricted to royal courts
Rising above religion, Hindu and Muslim artists practiced music together
e: In Kashi’s tradition, Muslim maestros participating in festivals at Sankatmochan and Balaji temples exemplified communal harmony.

q: In what context do "Iran-Iraq" appear in the chapter?
o: In the context of the ancient history of reed-based wind instruments like shehnai
As a filming location for Sulochana
As names of rivers in Dumraon
e: Iran and Iraq are referenced in relation to the antiquity of reed-based wind instruments and the "Nay" / "Shahe-Nay" tradition.

q: What has the author called "the school of culture" (sanskriti ki pathshala)?
e: The author calls Kashi the school of culture, revered in scriptures as Anandkanan where even death is considered auspicious.

q: What does the word "tasir" used in the chapter mean?
e: "Tasir" means effect or impact; Khan Sahib prayed for such impact in his notes that listeners would shed genuine tears.

q: In what sense is the word "neyamat" used in the chapter?
e: "Neyamat" means a divine blessing or gift; Khan Sahib regarded a true musical note as God’s greatest blessing.

q: What did Bismillah Khan mean by "anganh aansu" (unhewn/unfeigned tears)?
o: Genuine, spontaneous tears straight from the heart
e: "Anganh aansu" refers to unpolished, genuine, spontaneous tears—like true pearls—evoked by deep musical emotion.

q: Regarding which Muharram tradition in Kashi was Bismillah Khan deeply sensitive?
o: Wearing new clothes for ten days
Observing ten days of mourning and playing the nauha standing on the 8th day
Holding shehnai contests for ten days
Playing after bathing in the Ganga
e: During the ten days of Muharram he refrained from playing ragas, and on the 8th day he walked eight km playing the mournful nauha.

q: Which specific place does Yatindra Mishra mention for Amiruddin’s musical practice (riyaz)?
o: The Naubaatkhana at the threshold of the Balaji Temple
e: Amiruddin and his maternal uncles practiced the shehnai early in the morning at the Naubaatkhana on the Balaji Temple threshold.

q: According to the text, what was Dumraon’s foremost claim to recognition in relation to shehnai?
o: It had the largest music university
The Taj Mahal is situated there
Bharat Ratna ceremonies were held there
It is Bismillah Khan’s birthplace and the source of narkat grass
e: Dumraon is notable for two reasons: it is Bismillah Khan’s birthplace, and narkat grass for shehnai reeds grows along its Son river.

q: Which specific musical forms are associated with Rasoolan Bai and Batoolan Bai in the chapter?
e: Rasoolan Bai and Batoolan Bai were famed for singing tappa, thumri, and dadra, which captivated young Amiruddin.

q: Who wrote works on music and literature such as "Sur ki Baradari" and "Yaar Julahe"?
e: Yatindra Mishra wrote "Girija", "Sur ki Baradari" (on Ustad Bismillah Khan), and "Yaar Julahe" (on Gulzar).

q: Which ancient city is referred to as "Anandkanan" in the chapter?
e: Describing the cultural glory of Kashi, the chapter refers to it as "Anandkanan", a living abode of culture.

q: What did Bismillah Khan’s regular presence at the Sankatmochan Temple music festival symbolize?
o: He went solely to earn money
He went only to meet foreign guests
He was appointed manager of the temple
He was deeply integrated into Kashi’s communal harmony and musical culture
e: Khan Sahib’s indispensable presence at the five-day Sankatmochan Hanuman Jayanti music festival exemplified Kashi’s shared culture.

q: Between migrating to glamorous cities and staying in Kashi, what did Bismillah Khan prioritize throughout his life?
o: Staying in Kashi in the proximity of Ganga Maiya
e: Bismillah Khan believed his music and life were incomplete without Kashi and Ganga Maiya, so he never left Kashi.

q: Which humble trait of Bismillah Khan repeatedly shines through in the chapter?
o: Considering himself a lifelong student of music even at eighty
e: Even at eighty and after winning the Bharat Ratna, he maintained that he was still praying to God for one true musical note.

q: Of which city’s cultural identity are "Mangalagauri" and "Kashi Vishwanath" mentioned as integral parts?
e: Kashi Vishwanath, Balaji Temple, Sankatmochan, and the Ganga ghats are integral to the cultural identity of Kashi.

q: What quality of Bismillah Khan does the "musical kachori" episode highlight?
o: His artistic sensibility that found music even in everyday sounds
e: Even in the sizzle of Kulsum’s kachori, he heard musical ascent and descent, showing how deeply music permeated his perception.

q: "Crazy girl, I received the Bharat Ratna for my shehnai, not for my lungi." — What trait of Bismillah Khan’s character is revealed by this remark?
o: Simplicity, humility, and devotion to art
e: This remark proves that even after winning global honours, Khan Sahib lived with utter simplicity above outward show, valuing art above all.

q: If a musician wishes to play the melodious shehnai, which two distinctions of Dumraon will they always remember?
o: Birthplace of the shehnai maestro and the narkat grass used for reeds
Its cinema halls and sweet shops
e: The chapter notes that narkat grass for shehnai reeds grows along the Son river in Dumraon, and it is also Ustad Bismillah Khan’s birthplace.

q: In Amiruddin’s childhood, music existed from the sizzle of kachori to the path to Balaji Temple. What does this context imply?
o: He wandered the streets all day
Formal training alone is not enough; a sensitive musical environment shapes an artist
Rasoolan Bai was his formal music teacher
e: Rasoolan-Batoolan’s singing and Kashi’s vibrant cultural surroundings played a vital role in awakening Amiruddin’s musical sensibility.

q: During the ten days of Muharram, Bismillah Khan refrained from playing ragas and walked eight km playing the nauha on the 8th day. Which human aspect does this reveal?
o: His uncles forbade him from playing
He grew tired of music for ten days
He played only during Hindu festivals
He deeply respected the sanctity of grief and faith
e: Since shehnai is an auspicious instrument, abstaining from ragas during the mourning of Imam Hussain reflects his deep faith and sensitivity.

q: When people advised Bismillah Khan to leave Kashi for Mumbai or other big cities, he refused. What was the primary reason for his decision?
o: Kashi held Ganga Maiya, Baba Vishwanath, Balaji Temple, and his ancestral roots
Mumbai had no audience for shehnai
e: For Khan Sahib, Kashi was not merely a city but his spiritual and cultural lifeblood, without which he could not imagine his life.

q: What psychology drove young Amiruddin to take the lane past Rasoolan Bai and Batoolan Bai’s house on his way to the Balaji Temple?
o: Their melodious singing gave him immense joy and musical inspiration
e: Desire to hear the melodious voices of the two singer sisters drew young Amiruddin to pass through their lane every day.

q: "My Lord, grant me just one true note" — Praying this even at the age of eighty reveals which attitude of Bismillah Khan?
o: He thought he had forgotten the shehnai
Artistic pursuit is infinite and a true devotee remains humble and eager to learn throughout life
He wanted to show disciples how religious he was
e: A true artist never claims perfection; until the very end of life, he retains the humility and yearning to refine his art.

q: If a student reads the episode of Amiruddin collecting money for cinema tickets, what insight does it give about the boy?
o: He possessed childlike innocence, love for art, and appreciation for beauty
e: Collecting two paise from relatives for Sulochana’s film and finding music in kachoris reflect his simple, joyful, art-loving childhood.

q: Why did the author title the chapter "Naubaatkhane mein Ibaadat"? Choose the most accurate reason.
o: Because for him, practicing the shehnai in the naubaatkhana was itself true worship of God
Because Bismillah Khan prayed inside a temple
Because Naubaatkhana was the name of a mosque
Because it was the first chapter of his autobiography
e: A Muslim maestro’s musical devotion at the temple’s naubaatkhana transcends religious boundaries and becomes pure worship (ibaadat).

q: Based on the text, if Kashi were personified, which two streams appear to flow harmoniously together in it?
o: Classical music tradition and communal/religious harmony
e: In Kashi, the Ganga, Vishwanath, Sankatmochan, Balaji Temple, and Ustad Bismillah Khan’s devotion create a confluence of music and communal harmony.

q: Even during concerts in other cities or abroad, why did Bismillah Khan sit facing the direction of Kashi?
o: He had no sense of direction
The stage was always arranged that way
It symbolized his deep reverence for Kashi Vishwanath, Balaji, and his teachers
Sound did not carry in other directions
e: Turning his shehnai toward Kashi Vishwanath and Balaji even when away reflects his deep gratitude and spiritual bond with Kashi.

q: "Why is Dumraon remembered in the world of the shehnai?" — What would be the most complete answer?
o: Only because there are shehnai factories there
Because a huge Muharram fair was held there
Because Kashi Vishwanath temple is located there
Because it is Bismillah Khan’s birthplace and the narkat grass for shehnai reeds grows there by the Son river
e: Dumraon holds twin importance: Bismillah Khan was born there, and the narkat grass vital for shehnai reeds grows on its Son riverbanks.

q: When his disciple pointed out his torn lungi despite winning the Bharat Ratna, what was she really concerned about?
o: That a celebrity’s outward appearance should match the prestige of his awards
e: The disciple felt a Bharat Ratna laureate should dress impressively, whereas Khan Sahib cared only for the purity of his musical notes.

q: Amiruddin striking a stone on the ground right when his uncle hit the "sam" indicates what?
o: His natural and sharp grasp of rhythm, beat, and sam right from childhood
A habit of playing with stones
e: Even at age six without knowing formal raga theory, applauding precisely at the sam with a stone shows his innate musical genius.

q: Why did the author mention that shehnai finds no reference in Vedic history or "Sangeet Raag Kalpadrum"?
o: To show how the shehnai evolved later in tradition yet rose to become supreme ("Shahe-Nay") among wind instruments
To prove shehnai is not played in India
e: Using historical context, the author shows that though newer than the flute, the shehnai rose through its sweetness to become "Shahe-Nay".

q: To experience Pakka Mahal’s malai baraf, Kulsum’s kachori, and a musical atmosphere together, which context in the chapter is most relevant?
o: Bismillah Khan’s nostalgic memories and love for Kashi
e: Reminiscing about old Kashi, Khan Sahib fondly recalls Pakka Mahal’s malai baraf, Kulsum’s kachoris, and his youthful cinema outings.

q: Bismillah Khan’s life teaches that what is greater than religious orthodoxy?
o: Art, human love, and communal harmony
e: Being a devout Muslim who revered Vishwanath, Balaji, and the Ganga shows that art and humanity transcend sectarian walls.

q: "Seeing musical ascent and descent in the sizzle of kachori in hot ghee" — What mindset of Bismillah Khan does this imagery reflect?
o: His entire consciousness was steeped in music
He learned music just to eat kachoris
e: For a devotee whose consciousness is wholly immersed in music, every sound of daily life resonates with notes and rhythm.

q: Why was the Sankatmochan music festival considered incomplete without Khan Sahib?
o: Because he owned the sound system
Because he was the living embodiment of Kashi’s Ganga-Jamuni culture and the soul of the shehnai
Because he was the temple priest
e: Bismillah Khan’s performance in the temple courtyard was both a pinnacle of music and an emblem of Kashi’s syncretic heritage.

q: "Even death is considered auspicious in Kashi" — For what purpose has the author invoked this traditional belief?
o: To describe cremation grounds in Kashi
To show that Kashi is not merely a place, but a cultural sanctuary that gives meaning to life and death
e: By invoking Kashi’s ancient glory, the author illuminates how deeply spiritual and inseparable Khan Sahib’s bond with Kashi was.

q: What role did his maternal uncles Sadiq Hussain and Alibakhsh play in Amiruddin’s journey to becoming Bismillah Khan?
o: They gave young Amiruddin early training, a practice environment, and the family musical heritage
They kept him away from the shehnai
They only gave him money for movies
They sent him back to Dumraon
e: Under his uncles’ guidance at the Balaji temple’s naubaatkhana in Kashi, Amiruddin imbibed the discipline of shehnai riyaz.

q: If an artist forgets their birthplace and early mentors after gaining fame, what contrasting lesson does this chapter offer?
o: One should forget the past after success
Staying connected to one’s roots, mentors, and simplicity even at the pinnacle is true greatness
Art flourishes only in big cities
One should stop practicing after winning awards
e: Even after winning the Bharat Ratna, Khan Sahib’s abiding love for Dumraon, Kashi, and his uncles exemplifies true greatness.

q: Why was Bismillah Khan so fearful of a "cracked note" (phata sur)?
o: Because audiences threw stones at him
Because he considered the musical note his worship, honour, and the very essence of life
Because he was taking an exam
e: For Khan Sahib, purity of note mattered far more than clothes or worldly goods; a cracked note meant a flaw in his devotion.

q: Which characteristic of Yatindra Mishra’s writing style is clearly visible in the chapter?
o: Overly dense and purely Sanskritized diction
Natural, intimate, and poetic blend of Hindi, Urdu, and Banarasi regional words
e: Words like "ibaadat", "riyaz", "naubaatkhana", "pakka mahal", and "kachori" infuse the prose with the living flavour of Banaras.

q: What practical reason behind calling the shehnai the champion of auspicious sound emerges from the text?
o: Its sound is sweet, soulful, and deeply moving at temples and auspicious occasions
It makes a loud harsh noise
Anyone can play it without training
e: The soulful and melodious resonance produced through its reed makes the shehnai the "Shahe-Nay" among all wind instruments.

q: What was the author’s purpose in opening the narrative with a scene of Kashi around 1916–1922?
o: To make readers memorize historical dates
To portray the milieu in which seeds of music were unconsciously sprouting in young Amiruddin
e: The author shows how Kashi’s mornings, temples, and singers were shaping Amiruddin even before he knew what a "raga" meant.

q: Why did the author mention "Geeta Bali" and "Sulochana" in the context of Bismillah Khan’s life?
o: To prove he was a film director
To highlight his relatable, joyful, and ordinary human side alongside his saintly devotion
To point out flaws in his music
e: Alongside being a great maestro, his love for kachori, malai baraf, and cinema reveals his warm, ordinary human nature.

q: "Two paise from mamu, two from mausi, two from nani" — Which quality of Amiruddin is reflected in this detail?
o: Childlike resourcefulness toward his wish and the affection of his family
e: Affectionately gathering two paise each from elders for his little wish shows both his resourcefulness and his family’s warmth.

q: With which city’s lifestyle are the words "adab" (courtesy) and "tahzeeb" (refinement) associated in the chapter?
e: Kashi’s lanes, people, temples, mosques, music, and food together cultivate a distinctive culture of courtesy and refinement.

q: According to Bismillah Khan’s life example, why can music not be confined within religious boundaries?
o: Because music is merely instrument noise
Because a true note is divine worship that unites hearts across all faiths
Because religion has no place for music
Because instruments are made in factories
e: Bismillah Khan’s playing at the temple threshold and praying for pure notes in namaz proves music is a universal language uniting all.
